children: Decline in foreign currency assets and gold holdings accounts for most of the weekly fall, RBI data shows

India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by USD 14.21 billion to USD 705.34 billion in the week ended 13 November, according to the latest data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Total reserves stood at USD 719.55 billion in the previous week ended 6 November.
The decline was led by a fall in foreign currency assets (FCAs) and gold reserves, which together accounted for most of the weekly reduction.

FCAs, the largest component of the reserves, fell by USD 7.90 billion to USD 583.45 billion during the reported week. Expressed in dollar terms, FCAs include the impact of appreciation or depreciation in non-US currencies such as the euro, pound and yen held in the reserves.
“There was dollar sale of USD 1.57 billion and rest is revaluation loss led by gold,” said Gaura Sen Gupta, Chief Economist at IDFC First Bank.

Gold reserves declined by USD 6.18 billion to USD 98.61 billion during the week. Special drawing rights (SDRs) fell by USD 92 million to USD 18.52 billion, while India’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) decreased by USD 32 million to USD 4.76 billion, the RBI data showed.
India’s foreign exchange reserves are now around USD 80.4 billion below their all-time high of USD 785.7 billion, recorded in the week ended 4 September.
The record level followed significant foreign currency inflows through a special concessional swap scheme for diaspora deposits.
In the previous week ended 6 November, reserves had increased, primarily due to a USD 2.205 billion rise in gold holdings.
Rupee Under Pressure From Rising US Treasury Yields
The rupee remained under pressure during the reported week amid rising yields on US Treasury securities.
On 12 November, the Indian currency closed 0.37 per cent lower at 94.04 against the US dollar. Dealers cited dollar purchases by state-run banks ahead of the release of Consumer Price Index data.
The rupee has depreciated by 3.02 per cent so far in calendar year 2026, while it has appreciated by 2.31 per cent in financial year 2026-27 so far.
The weekly movement in reserves reflects changes in foreign currency holdings and the valuation of assets, including gold and non-US currencies.
